feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (60 trials, 0 completions) showed all runs ending off track, with max error at 0.062 to 0.066 m against the 0.06 m limit, progress 0.23 (oval), 0.14 (s-bend) and 0.10 (slalom), and steering oscillation only about 0.13 to 0.15. The robot drifts off the line before covering the course, so the bottleneck is steering authority and anticipation rather than jitter. Because the controller was tuned for this drift, I raised kp and kd and lowered base_speed. If the next race shows max_error still at or above 0.06 m with progress under 0.3 on the slalom, the drivetrain is the bottleneck: keep wheel_track at 0.10 m and reduce mass further, or move the body length down to 0.12 m to lower yaw inertia more. If line_loss_events concentrate on the slalom while progress is high, the 16 mm footprint is over-blurring the signal; try sensor_size 0.012 m and keep the forward offset of 0.06 m. If the run finishes some tracks but steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, the cause is over-correction at the new gain, so return to a wider wheel_track (0.12 m) rather than changing sensors.
requested_changes: If max_error on the s-bend or slalom stays at or above 0.06 m with progress under 0.3, lower body_length from 0.14 m to 0.12 m and mass from 0.6 kg to 0.5 kg to cut yaw inertia further, since iteration 0 shows drift before the course is covered.

If line_loss_events are above 1 concentrated on the slalom while progress is high, set sensor_size to 0.012 m to reduce blur on the sharpest bends, keeping the forward offset of 0.06 m, since iteration 0 showed line losses at 1.0 to 1.55 per run.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with no line losses, return wheel_track to 0.12 m to lower turn rate, since the current gain increase may be over-correcting, not the sensors.
